newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria M1 rises 28 pct, M2 up 107 pct Jan31-Feb7.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria M1 rises 28 pct, M2 up 107 pct Jan31-Feb7.

text.p: Bulgarian M1 money supply rose to 302.9 billion levs on February 7 from 237 billion levs on January 31 and M2 surged to 3,889 billion levs from 1,880.4 billion levs, preliminary central bank figures showed.

Total broad money rose 108.6 percent to 4,211.1 billion levs in the week to February 7 as lev-denominated broad money increased 8.8 percent to 728.9 billion levs and dollar-denominated broad money jumped 158.1 percent to 3,482.2 billion levs.

"The vast increase of M2 and broad money was due mostly to the sharp dollar rise, which boosted the lev price of the dollar-denominated component of money supply," a central bank official told Reuters.
The dollar rose to 2608.40 levs on February 7 from 1021.90 a week earlier in the central bank daily dollar fix used in the calculations.
Hard currency-denominated deposits of companies totalled $740.2 million on February 7, up from $696.2 million a week earlier.
Foreign currency-denominated deposits of individuals however fell by $28.2 million to $474.4 million in the week ending February 7, figures showed.
Lev-denominated deposits of individuals edged down to 75.7 billion levs on February 7 from 76.8 billion levs on January 31.
